summary: Grafton County ground site: a fire lookout cab on a concrete foundation from 1940, last used 1948 and burned in the 1950s; the foundation remains on the summit.

facts.design: Fire lookout cab on a concrete foundation; the FFLA lists the site as ground, not a tower
facts.status_note: Cab burned in the 1950s; the concrete foundation remains at the summit

access.note: Reached on foot by the Appalachian Trail; no restriction is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: The final stretch crosses slab rock to the summit and foundation; AT access is about two minutes below the summit

events.note: Fire lookout cab built on a concrete foundation (Willhite)
Willhite gives 1948 as the final year of use; the source does not say who staffed it

evidence.supports: listed as a ground site, not a tower, in Grafton County, and marked gone
cab built in 1940 on a concrete foundation
evidence.quote: In 1940, a fire lookout cab was built on a concrete foundation.

evidence.supports: 1948 was the final year of use
evidence.quote: In 1948 was the final year of use.

evidence.supports: the cab was burned in the 1950s
after the 1938 hurricane the CCC built several new lookouts, guard stations, trails and roads
evidence.quote: Several new lookouts, guard stations, trails and roads were constructed by the CCC (Civilian Conservation Corps) at this time.

evidence.supports: the 1938 hurricane context for the CCC work
evidence.quote: The 1938 Hurricane blew down thousands of acres of forest

evidence.supports: the concrete foundation is tied to the CCC-era period
evidence.quote: The concrete foundation of the lookout on the summit of Mount Garfield is a stark reminder of that period.

evidence.supports: Appalachian Trail access about two minutes below the summit
evidence.quote: AT Access: Trail 2 minutes below the summit

evidence.supports: the last stretch is slab rock to the summit and old foundation
evidence.quote: The final hundred feet or so is on slab rocks to reach the summit and former fire lookout foundation.

evidence.supports: the outhouse was still standing north of the summit, hidden by balsam fir
evidence.quote: still standing and is a short distance north of the summit hidden by balsam fir trees

notes_for_editor: Most dated detail (1940 cab, 1948 last use, 1950s burning, foundation today) rests on one source, Willhite. The White Mountain History article independently ties the foundation to the CCC-era work after 1938. No source names staffers or fires for this site, so none are written. The brief's record is consistent with the FFLA listing (ground, Grafton, gone). No photos added.
